question.text: An Offshore Fund that wishes to invest into India via the FVCI route obtains which of the following advantages compared to a generic foreign investor?

answer.text: Flexible entry/exit pricing, exemption from lock-in when the investee goes public, exemption from SEBI Takeover Code on certain transactions, and QIB status in capital markets

explanation.text: The Logic: A SEBI-registered FVCI gets: flexible entry/exit pricing (not bound by FEMA pricing guidelines), exemption from lock-in when the investee company lists (so they can exit post-IPO immediately), exemption from the SEBI Takeover Code on specified transactions, and QIB status for capital market purposes — all material regulatory benefits over plain FDI. The Trap: Options B, C, D are fabricated blanket exemptions that don't exist. The FVCI route has specific, defined benefits — not blanket. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C/D cover FVCI briefly. XIX-E tests the specific benefit list. Manager's Pro-Tip: If you raise a Cat III with significant foreign capital in unlisted or pre-IPO names, evaluate FVCI vs. FPI routing early — FVCI has superior exit flexibility for the private-market sleeve of a multi-strategy Cat III.
